'''''Desmodium canadense''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[legume]] family, [[Fabaceae]]. It is native to eastern North America. Its common names include '''showy tick-trefoil''', '''Canadian tick-trefoil''',<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 21 January 2018}}</ref> and '''Canada tickclover'''.<ref>[https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=25791 ''Desmodium canadense''.] Integrated Taxonomic Information System.</ref>

The plant is a perennial herb and grows in woods, [[prairie]]s, and disturbed habitat, such as roadsides. It is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]]. It is a [[larva]]l host plant for [[butterfly|butterflies]] such as the [[eastern tailed-blue]], [[Epargyreus clarus|silver-spotted skipper]], and [[Achalarus lyciades|hoary edge]]. The plant attracts butterflies and hummingbirds.<ref>[http://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=DECA7 ''Desmodium canadense''.] Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center. University of Texas, Austin.</ref> Flowers are pea-shaped, pink to purple in color, and bloom between July and September.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Desmodium canadense (Showy Tick-trefoil): Minnesota Wildflowers|url=https://www.minnesotawildflowers.info/flower/showy-tick-trefoil|access-date=2021-12-02|website=www.minnesotawildflowers.info|language=en}}</ref>

[[File:Desmodium canadense11.jpg|thumb|]]
''Desmodium canadense'' is being investigated as a possible source of [[bean pod mottle virus]] in [[soybean]] plants. As a carrier of the virus, it may be passing it to the [[bean leaf beetle]], which is passing it in turn to soybean crops.<ref>Krell, Rayda Kathryn (2002). ''Bean pod mottle virus ecology and management in Iowa'' (Thesis). [[ProQuest (identifier)|ProQuest]] 305571983</ref> This virus causes severe systemic [[Mottle|mottling]] and mild leaf puckering.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hopkins |first=John D. |last2=Mueller |first2=A. J. |date=1983-10-01 |title=Distribution of Bean Pod Mottle Virus in Arkansas Soybean as Related to the Bean Leaf Beetle, Cerotoma trifurcata, (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population 1 |url=https://academic.oup.com/ee/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/ee/12.5.1564 |journal=Environmental Entomology |language=en |volume=12 |issue=5 |pages=1564–1567 |doi=10.1093/ee/12.5.1564 |issn=1938-2936|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This can reduce seed size and pod set, which causes a decrease in crop yields.<ref>"Bean Leaf Beetle | Integrated Crop Management". ''crops.extension.iastate.edu''. Retrieved 2024-04-03.</ref>
